threads.body:
Bigger-picture concern about the approach, and I'd like it addressed in this PR rather than after.

Callback metadata cannot identify a `create_agent` root. When an agent is invoked from inside another agent's tool with the config forwarded, LangChain merges the caller's config over the inner agent's own, so `lc_agent_name` and `ls_integration` here describe the **outer** agent. That is why this PR has to reason about ancestry at all, and why nested agents end up unsupported. I checked every other field on the callback (`serialized` is `None`, `langgraph_checkpoint_ns` does not deepen at the nested root, `tags` and `kwargs["name"]` do not separate an agent from any other named runnable), and there is no signal that distinguishes them. LangSmith hits the same wall and works around it by reading pregel task events instead of callbacks, accepting a documented false positive.

The compiled graph's *own* bound config is never shadowed, though:

```python
create_agent(model, tools, name="inner").config
# {'metadata': {'ls_integration': 'langchain_create_agent', 'lc_agent_name': 'inner'}, ...}
```

So patching `Pregel.stream`/`astream` lets the graph announce itself on a context stack that the handler claims when the root run starts. That is ground truth instead of inference, and it removes the need for the ancestry heuristics entirely.

I put together a prototype: https://github.com/lmolkova/opentelemetry-python-genai/commit/81515bf6811da59e8f5c02e30492da2bbd186b93

With it, three-level nesting, same-named nested agents, async, streaming, unnamed agents and agents invoked without config forwarding all layer correctly, with no false positives for a named `RunnableLambda` or a plain subgraph invoked from a tool. It also deletes `create_agent_ancestry`, the `has_create_agent_marker` plumbing and these `ls_integration` / `lc_agent_name` branches, so it is close to net-neutral in size.

Please fold this into this PR. Merging the metadata-inference version first means we delete most of it in the follow-up, and the ancestry logic changes classification behavior in the meantime, so we would be shipping a regression risk for code we already plan to remove.

Note the prototype is exactly that - the tests for the removed inference still need dropping and the corpus tests reworking (separate comment).

They construct the callback handler directly and hand it a `MagicMock` telemetry handler, so what they assert is the internal shape of `invoke_local_agent` calls, not the telemetry a user gets. That makes them pass for classifications that produce no usable span, and it makes them break on any refactor of the handler's internals even when the emitted spans are unchanged.

+# Copyright The OpenTelemetry Authors
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+"""Identify ``create_agent`` graph invocations from outside the callback API.
+
+LangChain callbacks cannot tell a nested ``create_agent`` root apart from any
+other named runnable invoked inside a tool: the enclosing agent's ``config`` is
+merged over the inner agent's own, so ``lc_agent_name`` and ``ls_integration``
+in the *callback* metadata describe the outer agent. The compiled graph's own
+bound config is never shadowed, so this module reads the marker there and has
+each graph entry point announce itself on a context stack that the callback
+handler consults when the root run starts.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable, Iterator
+from contextvars import ContextVar
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any
+
+from opentelemetry.instrumentation.genai.langchain.operation_mapping import (
+    create_agent_graph_name,
+)
+
+_AGENT_NAME_ATTR = "_otel_genai_agent_name"
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _PendingAgent:
+    """An agent graph that has started running but whose root run is not seen yet."""
+
+    name: str
+    claimed: bool = False
+
+
+_pending: ContextVar[tuple[_PendingAgent, ...]] = ContextVar(
+    "otel_genai_pending_agents", default=()
+)
+
+
+def claim_agent() -> str | None:
+    """Return the announced agent name if this run is a create_agent graph root.
+
+    The announcement is made as the graph starts, so the first chain run to see
+    it is the graph's root. Only the innermost announcement is claimable, and
+    only once, so internal nodes fall through to metadata-based classification.
+    The root run's own name is not checked - ``with_config(run_name=...)``
+    renames it without making it any less of an agent.
+    """
+    pending = _pending.get()
+    if not pending:
+        return None
+    entry = pending[-1]
+    if entry.claimed:
+        return None
+    entry.claimed = True
+    return entry.name
+
+
+def _agent_name(graph: Any) -> str | None:
+    """Return the agent name a compiled graph identifies itself with, if any."""
+    marked = getattr(graph, _AGENT_NAME_ATTR, None)
+    if marked:
+        return str(marked)
+    return create_agent_graph_name(getattr(graph, "config", None))

"LangGraph" isn't an agent name - it's the framework's default graph name. `gen_ai.agent.name` is the name the application gave the agent, and semconv says to leave it unset and name the span plain `invoke_agent` when there isn't one.

The conformance scenario dropped `agent_name`, so it now asserts this placeholder and no longer covers a named agent.
